== PlayStation 2 OSD sound assets and the NRPN-127 loop ==
''Suggested page: PS2 → Sound / Audio Architecture → OSD Sound Assets and Sequences.''

The atmospheric boot chimes and background audio of the PlayStation 2's system menus (OSDSYS) are generated through Sony's SPU2 sound processor via SShd/SSbd sound banks and MIDI-like SSsq sequence files. Across all retail BIOS revisions from 1.00 J (2000) to 2.00 E (2004), the audio assets remained fundamentally consistent.

=== Sound banks (SShd / SSbd) ===
Analysis of the full BIOS corpus identifies '''five byte-distinct sound banks''' (representing 21 unique ADPCM audio streams and 18.49 seconds of total stored sound):

{| class="wikitable"
! Bank ID !! Name / Role !! Header + Body !! Contents !! Allocation / Location
|-
| '''B01''' || PS2 game-logo chord bank || 0x1E0 + 0x2C90 (0x2E70 bytes) || 5 effects, 1 sample (0.452 s) || Inline inside <code>rom0:PS2LOGO</code> (uploaded to SPU2 <code>0x5010</code>). Unchanged across all versions.
|-
| '''B02''' || PS1 shell instrument bank || 0x1220 + 0xA860 (0xBA80 bytes) || 4 programs, 3 VAG samples (1.710 s) || Version-6 <code>pBAV</code> in all PS1 shells, POPS, and PS2 <code>rom0:LOGO</code>.
|-
| '''B03''' || PS2 boot & ambience instruments || 0x4CA + 0x56F10 (0x573DA bytes) || 17 programs, 9 samples (14.131 s) || Packaged in <code>SNDIMAGE/SNDBOOTH</code> + <code>SNDBOOTB</code> (SPU2 <code>0x5010</code>). Inline inside <code>OSDSYS</code> in 1.00 J.
|-
| '''B04''' || PS2 OSD menu effects (14 entries) || 0x420 + 0xD480 (0xD8A0 bytes) || 14 effects, 7 samples (2.154 s) || Packaged in <code>SNDIMAGE/SNDOSDDH</code> + <code>SNDOSDDB</code> (SPU2 <code>0x85010</code>). Present in 1.50 devkit through 2.00 E.
|-
| '''B05''' || PS2 OSD menu effects (12 entries) || 0x3A0 + 0xD480 (0xD820 bytes) || 12 effects, 7 samples (2.154 s) || SCPH-10000 (1.00 J) only. Header declares 12 entries; body is byte-identical to B04.
|-
| '''S01''' || 1 kHz test sine (<code>1KSine.48</code>) || 0x4F0 bytes || 1 VAG (0.044 s, 48 kHz loop) || Standalone diagnostic sample inside <code>rom0:TESTSPU</code> (1.50 devkit through 2.00 E).
|}

=== The eight SSsq sequence scores ===
All eight SSsq sequences in OSDSYS play on bank '''B03 (slot 0)''' at a timing resolution of '''480 ticks per quarter note'''. The sound assets are copied to IOP buffers <code>0x1000</code> through <code>0x9000</code> and registered with driver command <code>0x5009</code>:

{| class="wikitable"
! Slot !! Sequence name !! Size !! Tempo !! Stored length !! Role and runtime trigger
|-
| 0 || '''SNDBOOTS''' || 0x1CC bytes || 90 BPM || 9.17 s (8 notes) || Normal boot opening sound; queued by OSDSYS (command <code>0x5014, 0</code>) when boot state is 1.
|-
| 1 || '''SNDTNNLS''' || 0x1A2 bytes || 90 BPM || 1.25 s (4 notes) || Opening-to-menu transition ("tunnel transition"); triggered at <code>0x21A880</code> and <code>0x21A940</code>.
|-
| 2 || '''SNDCLOKS''' || 0x64C bytes || 120 BPM || 300.00 s (126 notes) || Clock / main menu ambient soundtrack; triggered at <code>0x2299CC</code>, <code>0x229B44</code>, <code>0x22E94C</code>. Infinite loop.
|-
| 3 || '''SNDTM30S''' || 0x130 bytes || 90 BPM || 0.67 s (1 note) || "30-second timer cue" (program 60). Registered in asset table; no active play call found in OSDSYS [I].
|-
| 4 || '''SNDTM60S''' || 0x130 bytes || 90 BPM || 0.67 s (1 note) || "60-second timer cue" (program 70). Registered in asset table; no active play call found in OSDSYS [I].
|-
| 5 || '''SNDLOGOS''' || 0x130 bytes || 90 BPM || 0.67 s (1 note) || Byte-identical to <code>SNDTM30S</code>. Registered in OSDSYS (distinct from the game-logo chord).
|-
| 6 || '''SNDWARNS''' || 0x64D bytes || 110 BPM || 327.27 s (126 notes) || Red-screen warning opening; queued by OSDSYS (command <code>0x5014, 6</code>) when boot state is 4. Infinite loop.
|-
| 7 || '''SNDRCLKS''' || 0x1A2 bytes || 90 BPM || 1.19 s (4 notes) || CD-media transition; played when disc types 0x6C..0x6E are identified at <code>0x21A8FC</code>.
|}

=== The NRPN-127 infinite loop mechanism ===
Neither the clock ambience (<code>SNDCLOKS</code>) nor the warning ambience (<code>SNDWARNS</code>) is a finite musical track. Instead, both implement seamless, infinite loops driven by MIDI Non-Registered Parameter Numbers (NRPN):
* '''<code>SNDCLOKS</code>''':
** Plays a 19.00-second introductory passage.
** At tick 18,240, it sets NRPN MSB (Controller 99) to 20, followed by Data Entry (Controller 6) set to '''127'''.
** The sequence continues for another 281 seconds (up to tick 288,000, where NRPN 30 defines the loop end).
* '''<code>SNDWARNS</code>''':
** Plays a 19.64-second introductory passage.
** At tick 17,280, it sets NRPN 20, Data Entry (Controller 6) to '''127''', and loops at tick 288,000 (a 307.64-second loop).
* '''Driver behavior''': In Sony's <code>OSDSND</code> driver (IOP address <code>0x19B9C</code>), Controller 6 with value '''127''' is interpreted as a command to '''loop indefinitely'''. The driver branches back to the loop marker rather than terminating. Thus, the ambient soundtrack never ends naturally, sustaining until interrupted by user navigation or game launch.

=== Game logo chord (R01) vs SNDLOGOS ===
The sound played when the "PlayStation 2" logo appears on game launch is '''not <code>SNDLOGOS</code>'''. It is an executable-triggered chord (routine <code>0x1075C8</code> in 2.00 <code>PS2LOGO</code>) that issues five simultaneous effect commands (indices 0 through 4) on bank '''B01'''. These play the single 0.452 s source sample across five distinct voices at pitches 3090, 3046, 2298, 4096, and 3068 (SPU units) with stereo panning and reverb.

''Source: [https://github.com/NamasteJasutin/PSXBootInspectionTool PSXBootInspectionTool], notes/research/sound_inventory.md §1–§4.''
